newsitem.title: THAILAND: INTERVIEW-Stainless steel demand on rise in Asia.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Stainless steel demand on rise in Asia.

text.p: The head of Thailand's biggest stainless steel producer said on Monday that despite a global slowdown in 1996, the demand for stainless steel in the Asia-Pacific region was far from being saturated.

Prayudh Mahagitsiri, chairman and chief executive officer of Thainox Steel Ltd, told Reuters that the demand from members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) would grow to 235,000 tonnes per year in 2000 from 152,000 tonnes in 1995.
ASEAN comprises Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
Stainless steel demand in China was expected to reach 885,000 tonnes in 2000, up from 550,000 tonnes last year.
"I have strong confidence for the prospect of this industry in the region, and Thailand in particular," Prayudh said in an interview.
Strong economic growth and the size of the population in the region would propel growth in stainless steel demand.
He said that during the next two decades, the Asia-Pacific region would become the most important zone for stainless steel consumption.
"People here are trying to improve their standard of living. When people are more affluent, they tend to use more holloware (pots, kettles)," he said.
"The expanding infrastructure and construction projects in the region will also increase the demand for stainless steel," he said.
For Thailand, Prayudh expects strong demand to continue. Consumption grew by 15 percent in the past five years and would continue to grow strongly, although at a slower rate.

He said the current annual demand for stainless steel consumption in Thailand was about 100,000 tonnes. Demand was likely to increase to 133,000 tonnes per year in 1998 and almost 160,000 tonnes in 2000.
Prayudh said Thainox Steel recently expanded annual capacity to 160,000 tonnes from 60,000 tonnes. The new capacity will be onstream by May, 1997.

"That means a year or two after the new capacity is achieved, we still can export stainless products," he said. "Our main market would be ASEAN countries. We also eye China as the country with a lot of potential."
Prayudh said he did not rule out the possibility of further expanding Thainox capacity, but declined to elaborate.
"It all depends on the situation in the future," he said.
